title: Splitting off units when the sharp group completion is torsion free
statement: Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, with torsion-free group completion $P^{\rm gp}$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Put $U=P^\times$ and $B=P/U$, identifying elements that differ by a unit. Assume that $B^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free. Then there are an integer $s\geq0$ and a monoid isomorphism $P\simeq B\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ under which the quotient $P\to B$ is the first projection. Equivalently, $P\to B$ admits a monoid section $j:B\to P$ and $(b,u)\mapsto j(b)+u$ is an isomorphism $B\oplus U\simeq P$, with $U\simeq\mathbf Z^s$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102, local lift comparison; agent algebraic refinement with the explicit extra hypothesis on the sharp group. Not asserted for arbitrary fine torsion-free monoids.

proof.text: Write $G=P^{\rm gp}$, $U=P^\times$, $B=P/U$, and $H=B^{\rm gp}$. Apply [lem-trf-integral-sharpening-group-exactness] to the integral monoid $P$: $B$ is integral, the induced $\pi:G\to H$ is surjective with kernel $U$, and a finite generating list of $P$ maps to group generators of $H$. Such a list exists since $P$ is fine. Thus $H$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102, algebraic refinement with the stated torsion-free sharp group hypothesis; finite-basis input VI 3.7(a), p.75.

proof.text: The assumed torsion-freeness of $H$ and [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] give a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis of $H$. Apply [lem-trf-group-section-monoid-product] with $Q=B$ and its quotient map $q$: Step 1 supplies integrality, surjectivity and the kernel equality. It gives a monoid section $j:B\to P$ and inverse isomorphisms $F(b,u)=j(b)+u$ and $E(p)=(q(p),p-j(q(p)))$, with $qF(b,u)=b$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102, algebraic refinement with the stated torsion-free sharp group hypothesis; finite-basis input VI 3.7(a), p.75.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-generators] to a finite generating list of $P$. It gives finite generation of $U$, and torsion-freeness of $U$ from the assumed torsion-freeness of $G$. By [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free], $U$ has a finite integer basis of some length $s\geq0$. Unique basis coordinates give an additive isomorphism $a:U\simeq\mathbf Z^s$, whose inverse takes $(n_i)$ to the sum of $n_i$ times the basis vectors.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102, algebraic refinement with the stated torsion-free sharp group hypothesis; finite-basis input VI 3.7(a), p.75.

proof.text: Define $e:P\to B\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ by $e(p)=(q(p),a(p-j(q(p))))$, namely $(1_B\oplus a)\circ E$. Its inverse is $(b,z)\mapsto j(b)+a^{-1}(z)$ by the inverse equations of Step 2. Its first coordinate is $q(p)$. Thus $e$ gives the first formulation, while $j,F,a$ give the equivalent formulation with the same integer $s$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, pp.100,102, algebraic refinement with the stated torsion-free sharp group hypothesis; finite-basis input VI 3.7(a), p.75.
